body: Work item 'Have writers declare only the locks their tests show' (and B4/B105): skills/converge/prompts/test-verify.md:29-31 tells the verifier its brief names 'the locks the test holds, and the locks its test support declares', and judges each lock against 'the test's own code and its test support alone'. The brief stage_verify files is built by scripts/tests::test_verify_line -> declarations_text(item, s, old), which reads only the plan scenario's, the state record's, and the tests item's own locks: it never reads support_lock_map/test_support_locks and never reads the locks pool. Where the test's own list is empty and a test support file it lists declares a lock, declarations_text prints 'It holds no lock, so it is isolated.' (scripts/tests:5420-5421), which is false for the effective declaration the run, the lock check, and the window use (live_tests effective_locks). Its sibling scenario_brief prints 'Locks its test support declares: ...' (scripts/tests:4741-4742) and speed_brief passes entry['support_locks']; the verify brief does not. stage_verify also never calls live_tests, so a lock a flaky fixer's locks item added (B105 lists 'the verify brief' among its readers) never shows in the verifier's brief. Entry point: tests tasks --stage verify -> stage_verify -> test_verify_brief -> test_verify_line -> declarations_text; the outcome the prompt promises (the verifier sees the test support's locks) is reached only in part. Scope: caused by the change (the verify brief text and test-verify.md were both rewritten this sprint).

Entry A9 (a message an agent acts on says what is not so). Trigger: tests tasks --stage write files a test support task for a file whose locks the scenario list's test_support_locks or a locks item records, e.g. [{name: notice, mode: exclusive}]. Path: cmd_tasks -> stage_write -> stage_test_support -> test_support_brief (scripts/tests:5129-5146). The brief's first line says 'Locks it declares: notice (exclusive)', then lists each scenario whose test uses the file through 'lines += ["- %s" % scenario_brief(s) for s in scenarios]' (line 5140), which passes no support_locks, so scenario_brief (4739-4744) prints 'It holds no lock, so it is isolated.' for every scenario with no own locks. Harm: the brief tells the test support writer that tests which take this file's locks are isolated, contradicting decision:tests-isolated-unless-declared ('every test that lists the file as its test support takes them') and the notes' scenario_brief change ('where its test support declares any, Locks its test support declares: ...'); the writer records the file's locks from that brief. Scope: caused by this sprint (the base brief named resources; the isolation sentence and the support_locks parameter are new in this change).

Entry A9 (a message an agent acts on says what is not so), and B4's ruling that task briefs 'name the locks it holds and its test support's locks'. Trigger: tests tasks --stage verify files a verifier for a tests item whose test lists a test support file that declares locks (scenario list test_support_locks or a locks item keyed by the path), and the test declares none of its own. Path: cmd_tasks -> stage_verify -> test_verify_brief -> test_verify_line -> declarations_text (scripts/tests:5416-5421): 'entry = {"locks": declared_locks(s, old)}; recorded_declarations(entry, item); if entry["locks"]: ... return ["It holds no lock, so it is isolated."]'. It reads the test's own locks alone and never the support locks, so the verifier's brief says the test is isolated while its effective locks (live_tests' effective_locks, which run, the round header, and the lock check use) hold the support file's names. Harm: the verifier, which checks the locks the test's code shows, is told the test is isolated and holds nothing from its test support, which is false. Scope: caused by this sprint (declarations_text was rewritten for locks in this change).

Class C1, improvement I1 reached only in part. I1 promises: 'declared_locks and merged_locks are the one reader every site calls, so a later change to the declaration edits one function.' Entry: tests tasks --stage verify -> stage_verify -> test_verify_line -> declaration_changes (scripts/tests:5372-5381), which reads the declaration precedence itself: 'planned = next((record["locks"] for record in (s, old) if isinstance(record.get("locks"), list)), None)', the same first-record-holding-a-list rule declared_locks (1197-1199) implements, kept as a second copy beside declarations_text (5417), which calls declared_locks(s, old) over the same two records. Where the outcome ends: a change to how a declaration is read (the precedence of plan over scenario list, or the record shape) must edit declaration_changes as well as declared_locks, the cost I1 says it removes. body: Work item 'Route a flaky test through its round's window' (notes: 'A stopped round's reproduction (fix.md step 9) uses the round's order seed and worker count too'). fix.md step 9 sends a stopped--silence defect whose tests all pass alone to 'route the cause as the flaky route in step 3 says'. That route opens with '.ok-planner/bin/tests window --sprint ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>', and verify.md's lock and found-none checks both 'Rerun ... tests window ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>'. For a stopped round there is no usable window: the defect's test field is 'stopped--silence', which cmd_window refuses ('round %d of %s planned no test %s', scripts/tests cmd_window), and each hung test the round left is recorded by scripts/tests::unreported with seconds None and not_run, so cmd_window refuses it too ('records no run of %s, so it has no window', via run_timed). Path: fix.md step 9 -> step 3 flaky route -> tests window (refuses) -> race/overload/found-none record -> verify.md flaky bullet -> 'Rerun tests window' (refuses) -> the check cannot hold, so the verifier sends the fix back. A suite defect has no send-back limit and never goes stuck (converge SKILL Loop 2), so a stopped round caused by a race between tests that pass alone has no route that a verifier can accept: the lock outcome the work item promises is not reached for step 9, and the fix loop re-files the same defect without end. Scope: caused by the change (step 9's reference to the flaky route and the window-based verifier checks are both new this sprint).

body: Entry A1 (stored state can end half-changed). Trigger: a docs stamp that stops after write_state for some docspecs and before review.record_closes, then is run again, the recovery this sprint names (notes, 'Record a documentation sprint's close in the ledger', Calls: 'A stamp that stops before its entry is run again'; the CEREMONY-ARCHIVE resume rule in skills/_sprint/shared.md). Path: scripts/docs:cmd_stamp -> read_state (each docspec the first pass already wrote) -> old_stamp = state['stamp'], now the closing commit itself (state['stamp'] = args.commit on the first pass) -> stale_until = parent_commit(args.commit) -> stale = stale_claims(state, committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)), quoted: 'stale = {claim["id"] for claim in stale_claims(state, set(committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)))}'; committed_between runs 'git diff --name-only <closing commit> <its parent>', so it lists every file the closing commit changed. -> ledger_after drops each previous claim whose id is in stale_ids. Harm: on the rerun, each claim the first pass kept whose file or sources the closing commit changed (a doc comment an in-code docspec's run wrote that another docspec's claim cites as a source, say) is now stale and is dropped from the docspec's claim ledger, though an uninterrupted stamp keeps it; the rerun pass also feeds the half-written states to later_commits_bearing through planned_ledgers. So a stopped-and-rerun stamp leaves a claim ledger no complete run produces, and docs window's stale count and the next documentation sprint's checkers lose those claims. I202 fixes the doubled held claims on this rerun but not this. Scope: reached; the stale computation stood the same at the base, and this change makes the rerun the named recovery path for a stop before the ledger entry.

body: Artifact: decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window, which the work item 'Plan documentation from closing commits' makes true: 'It asks the owner about a change no such closing commit made'; the work item: 'An unexplained change is a change in the window to what the docspec describes that no listed closing commit made.' Code site: core.md {{DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT}} step 5 now defines it as 'a change in `git diff <stamp>` whose files no listed closing commit's `git show --name-only` names'. What the code does instead: it tests file overlap, not who made the change. Trigger: a docspec stamped at S; sprint A closes at Z and changes skills/foo/SKILL.md; an out-of-band commit Y after S also changes skills/foo/SKILL.md in a way the docspec describes. The cumulative git diff S shows the file changed, Z's name-only list names the file, so the planner counts Y's change as made by Z and returns no unexplained change. /plan-docs's Resolve step (SKILL.md section 3, 'A change no closing commit made') never asks the owner, and the writers describe Y's change with no owner answer, which the decision reserves to the owner (describe it or hold the docspec). The same step also says 'Name its commit' while defining the change from a cumulative diff, which carries no commit, so the planner has no stated way to find the commit it must name. Scope: caused by this sprint (the base step 5 read 'no sprint closed since the stamp made or explains', a judgment over the sprint documents; the file-overlap test is new).

Before (5743a8a): it returned (None, None) at once where .ok-planner/test-state.json did not stand as a file, so diagnose ran no carried tool in such a project. Trigger: a bootstrap candidate (no .ok-planner/) whose owner says yes at step 3, then aborts the plan at step 5; or any diagnose in a project with no scenario list. Old outcome: diagnose wrote nothing, and after an abort the project stayed a bootstrap candidate. New outcome: diagnose creates .ok-planner/.cache/ in a project that has no estate. The estate marker now stands after an abort, so the next /ok takes the project as integrated and skips the bootstrap question. toc_steps, which skips where ok_dir is absent, now also runs catalog-toc --check in that same diagnose. The notes' B23 lists 'one rewrite per converted file' and the issue, not a tool run in projects with no scenario list. Scope: caused by the change.

body: C2 under A3, from build fork i106 (t49). Trigger: an owner runs /ok on a project whose intake holds markdown issue files under .ok-planner/issues/ (or pre-4.0 tensions), and the conversion's import fails after its dry run passed, or a git mv inside move_all fails. Path: admin/true-up::convert_moving -> move_all, which calls record_archived([...placed files under history/issues/]) before any move (true-up:2811-2813), so the ledger .ok-planner/closed-records.jsonl gains one archived entry per file; the import (or the move) fails; move_back returns every file to .ok-planner/issues/ (true-up:2835) and the ledger keeps its entries, since it only appends and no verb clears one. Next /ok: conversion_refusals -> intake_migration_refusals computes held = [dst for _, dst in pairs if archive_held(dst)] (true-up:2799-2801) and refuses 'the closed-record ledger already lists <names> under .ok-planner/history/issues/'. Harm: the conversion can never run again, and while markdown issue files stand under .ok-planner/issues/ every .ok-planner/bin/issues verb refuses with reason layout, saying to run /ok, so the intake is unusable and /ok cannot clear it; the refusal tells the owner nothing they can do. The corpus decides only that the bookkeeping is written before the move (decision:archive-read-by-nothing: 'Each archive step writes the bookkeeping before it moves a file into the archive'); it does not decide that a held name whose file never landed refuses the same step's rerun. Scope: caused; the ledger, record_archived, and the held check are new in this sprint (absent at 5743a8a).

body: Reviewed the fix path a break found by /drive takes. /drive SKILL.md: 'the owner list files each defect the merge keeps in the intake as a category: defect issue, for the next /converge to fix'. The next /converge in defects mode takes it through the backlog; merge.md: 'Merge each real one with --field issue=<the issue id> and its source backlog.' The issue record and its backlog report carry no story, surface, or variant field. converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 6: '6. **Confirm, in drive and sprint mode.**', and scripts/review unconfirmed_drive_defects keeps only a defect whose source is 'drive' (or one a source=drive duplicate folds into). So a drive-found break fixed by /converge defects is closed fixed on a verifier's reading of the change alone, with no driver ever trying the story again. Probed in a scratch true-up of the working tree: filed issue probe-sketch-defect (category defect), review backlog added report i3 {area: backlog, issue: probe-sketch-defect, site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md} with no story field; by contrast a source=drive defect i2 got 'confirm: defect i2; story sketch-an-idea; surface skill:sketch; variant whole; ... confirm 1 of 1' from review drives --confirm. The story promises: each break the check finds is fixed, so a change that breaks a promise does not reach users unnoticed; decision one-confirm-driver-per-defect, Choice: 'A fix to a drive-found defect that its verifier accepts gets one confirm driver per defect ... the defect is confirmed only where every story it names succeeds, and is sent back otherwise'. Saw: the /drive then /converge defects route fixes a drive-found defect with no confirm driver, so a fix that leaves the story still broken closes the defect issue as fixed. In /converge drive mode the same break is caught again only because the new drive re-finds it as a separate source=drive defect. evidence: review backlog output '{"reports": [{"item": "i3", "issue": "probe-sketch-defect", "files": ["plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md"]}], "settled": []}'; review drives --confirm --dry-run listed only {"defect": "i2", "story": "sketch-an-idea"}.

[--schedule <recommended | groups-side-by-side | groups-one-at-a-time> --schedule-said ...]' and 'tests: [{"path", "name", "resources": [...], "reads": [...]}]' for run, forms the lock model retired.

Reviewed /converge (SKILL.md, merge.md, owner-list.md, scripts/review cmd_backlog) for a backlog of two category: defect issues that name one flaw. review backlog adds one report per issue (scripts/review:cmd_backlog). The merge folds the second onto the first's defect: merge.md step 3 'Where it is, add the report's hunt number to that defect's seen ... settle every report: tasks item set <report id> --state merged --note "<defect id>"', step 4 'Join reports of this hunt that name one flaw into one defect', and in sprint mode 'a report on the same flaw as a defect that carries an issue field ... settles onto it and adds no defect'; the defect is added with one '--field issue=<the issue id>'. owner-list.md closes issues only for 'every defect with an issue field that stands verified' and for 'every report with an issue field that the merge rejected'; it reads 'the rejected reports with an issue field, and the reports still open' and never a report at merged. So the folded issue's flaw is fixed and verified, yet its issue stays open as category: defect; the next /plan-sprint offers it to the owner at Frame as an open defect to pick, and a sprint that listed it ends certification with it still open. The story promises: defects found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment; saw: an issue whose defect the run fixed stays in the intake for the owner. Evidence: owner-list.md 'For every defect with an issue field that stands verified, close its issue as fixed: issues close <the issue id> --as fixed --fixed-by <the run's name>'; grep -n merged owner-list.md prints nothing.

In a scratch project (stack up --name find-and-fix-defects-def6eb1e, true-up), opened a converge ledger, filed one category: defect issue, ran review backlog and review merges --source backlog, recorded the backlog merge's count as merge.md's Count section says (area backlog, hunt 1), then ran analysis steps 1 to 4: review areas, review hunts --first, review merges --round, review tally. SKILL.md analysis step 4 says the tally prints 'for each area ... a decision: hunt while the area has had fewer than hunt.min hunts, stop: converged ..., stop: cap' and the return lists 'per area: hunts run, defects, ... and how the area stopped'. scripts/review:tally_report reads every merges item with no --areas filter, so the backlog pseudo-area appears as an area that 'hunts again', though review hunts never files a hunt for it and it never stops. The story promises: defects found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment; saw: the tally and the run's return tell the owner an area still hunts after the hunt loop ended. Evidence: review tally printed {'area': 'backlog', 'hunts': 1, 'latest_new': 1, 'defects': 2, 'estimate': None, 'missed': None, 'decision': 'hunt'} beside six file areas at 'stop: converged'; the next review hunts printed 'hunts: 0 task(s) over 0 area(s)'.

Then changed the product (--shout), window showed both reached; planned sprint 2 with usage a change item and api carrying the template's line 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' (SKILL.md section 5 keeps such a heading so the stamp moves it forward; core.md planner step 2 yields no item for an in-code docspec reached only through a References corpus artifact or the docspec file changing). Ran the boilerplate steps 5-8 as written. Divergence: doc-sprint-document.md step 7 runs a generator only through checker tasks: 'File checker tasks of up to six files each ... The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also runs its ## Generator command, where its Where starts in code: and that section names one.' A docspec with no item (or only drop items) gets no checker task, so its generator never runs, while Completion contract item 1 requires 'every docspec with a ## Generator command has its run recorded' and artifact-definitions.md says 'A documentation sprint runs the command, and the command must succeed.' Step 8 only says 'work each failure it names', naming no step that files the generator's checker. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands; the run as written cannot reach DOCS COMPLETE unaided. saw: evidence: '.ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-20-second.md' printed 'DOCS NOT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-20-second.md' / '- docspec:api names a generator, and no checker recorded its run', exit=2. body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's sign-off checklist (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md), the docspec and surface intent definitions (skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md), /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and scripts/docs. Drove .ok-planner/bin/docs window in a scratch project. A reference docspec can name a class under ## Lists that the surface intent's rules name but that has no line under ## Where each class is declared, and sign-off approves it. Then no documentation sprint can list that class's members or find a missing one, and the run still ends DOCS COMPLETE. The sign-off Lists rule asks only that 'each bullet names a class the surface intent names, live or as a delta of the sprint amends it', and the Declaring lines rule checks only that each existing line 'names a class the rules above it name'. No rule requires a declaring line for each class a reference docspec lists. The definition asks for lines only 'for each class of entry point'. Downstream, DOC-CHECK-PROMPT has the checker 'list every public element of each class the docspec's ## Lists names from the files the surface intent names as declaring it'. With no declaring file it lists nothing, so no 'missing: <element>' claim is ever recorded and the completion contract holds. /plan-docs SKILL.md step 2 admits 'the surface intent names no declaring file for the class, so the reference cannot list its members', yet 'An unmatched class leaves the status as it stands', so the run goes ahead, and the class goes back to a /plan-sprint whose checklist has no rule that fires on it. The story promises: 'my reference documentation [names] every element I made public ... so that a reader can depend on what the reference lists'. The artifact definition promises: 'The documentation sprint lists every public element of each class from the tree as it stands, starting from the files the surface intent names as declaring the class'. body: Reviewed the test planning procedure (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests.md) and the sort prompt (tests-sort.md) for a taken legacy folder, then ran the procedure's tool steps in a scratch project (tests offers, groups --take legacy:<folder>, a sort task's items, tests plan, tests tasks --stage write, the legacy tasks' work, tests ports, stamp, rules, rules take): those all worked. The divergence: tests.md step 2 files the sort tasks in the same step as the story and runtime planners, with no --after, and drains them together ('Where the sort list holds files, file one sort task per ten of them ... --brief "<the inputs line>; files: <the paths>"'. 'Drain.'), so sort agents run concurrently with the planners. Yet tests-sort.md Read step 2 tells the sort agent to read 'The scenarios the story planners and the runtime planner recorded: tasks item list --pool scenarios --json' and to sort 'It checks the outcome a recorded scenario states ... adopt, into that scenario'. When the sort agent runs before a story planner records its new scenario, it sees none, and adopts the legacy test 'into a scenario you record' under its own id; the assembly (scripts/tests, the adopted-into-new branch near line 2489) only turns a planner's new scenario into an adopt when the legacy item's scenario field names that new scenario's id, so the plan carries a new scenario and an adopt for one outcome, and a new test gets written beside the legacy test that already checks it, unless the plan-wide review happens to flag the duplicate. The story promises the owner keeps the tests that check what the product promises; decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically states: 'A planned new scenario a legacy test already checks adopts that test in place of a new one.' The procedure leaves that to a race and a judgment review; filing each sort task --after the story and runtime tasks (or a second drain) would make it hold. evidence: tests.md step 2 text quoted above; tasks file accepts --after (usage line: '[--after AFTER [AFTER ...]]'); in the scratch run, an adopt whose scenario id names no planner scenario assembled as its own scenario: 'scenarios: 0 keep, 0 new, 0 rewrite, 0 retire, 0 gap, 1 adopt'.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2a), the sprint execution boilerplate (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 6a), the test-speed, test-verify, and test-write prompts, the shared TEST-SPEED-JUDGING block, and the tests tool's speed verbs (slowest, tasks --stage speed, settled, stamp). The speed read at write time, in the build stages, and after a failed round, the median ranking under the lock bound, acceptances that outlive support changes, product-slow handling, and the verifier's same-outcome check all match the decisions. One divergence: an unsettled speed send-back returned to its last passing version is not carried to the next sprint. SKILL.md step 2a sends the test back with the reason 'return the test file to blob <the blob>, its last passing version: its speed rewrite did not settle, and the speed send-back stays open for the next sprint', and docs/testing.md says the same ('its send-back stays open for the next sprint to take up'). But the tests tool reads speed verdicts only from the current sprint's run and certification ledger (scripts/tests:2996 record_runs returns sibling(sprint, '-run.jsonl') and certification_ledger(root, sprint); speed_runs at 3030 and speed_rows/stage_speed at 5618/5705 read only those), and stamp writes no send-back into .ok-planner/test-state.json (scripts/tests:6062 state.update writes stamps, scenarios, unguarded, budget, inferred, kept, ranking, ranked_sprints, acceptances, reaches, test_support_locks; stamped_acceptances at 5965 keeps accepted verdicts alone). So once the sprint is archived, the next sprint's speed task brief (speed_brief, built from speed_sent_back(merged, sid) over the current sprint's runs only) carries no earlier send-back, and the reader starts with nothing of the waste found. The story promises: the suite sped up over the sprints the owner already runs; decision failed-speed-rewrite-returns-to-its-last-passing-version says 'its send-back stays open for the next sprint to take up' and its rationale 'The open send-back carries the waste the reader found to the next sprint's speed read.' Saw: nothing persists the open send-back across the sprint boundary; the waste a reader found is dropped, and the next sprint picks the test only if the ranking happens to select it, with a fresh brief. evidence: scripts/tests:2997 'return [run for run in (sibling(sprint, "-run.jsonl"), certification_ledger(root, sprint))'; scripts/tests:6062 state.update(...) has no send-back key; skills/converge/SKILL.md:122 'and the speed send-back stays open for the next sprint'.

body: Reviewed how a sprint's test stages fit the suite to the machine: the preflight (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md, Check 1) is the one step that measures this machine before a round and writes a lowered count to .ok-planner/.cache/tests-machine.json; the write stage that files it (scripts/tests help, line 475) says: 'It files no preflight where the plan's budget carries a preflight mark and equals the budget the scenario list records', and plan-sprint/tests.md step 4 (line 38) says: 'the plan carries the recorded budget, its preflight mark included, and the sprint's test stages run no preflight for a budget the plan leaves as recorded.' The mark is committed in .ok-planner/test-state.json and set by whichever machine's preflight last passed, while the machine record is per machine and git-ignored (ok-planner-CLAUDE.md line 609: deleting .ok-planner/.cache drops tests-machine.json, 'so the next bin/tests run runs the budget's worker count'). So on a second developer's machine, or this machine after its cache is dropped, no preflight and no budget planner runs while the budget stands unchanged, nothing measures the machine, and the first whole-suite round runs the budget's full count; only the flaky fixer lowers the count, after an overload round has failed tests. Under testing.enabled frozen no write stage files a preflight at all. The story promises: 'a way to have the suite's load fit what my machine can carry, run after run, so that a test fails for a fault in the product or the test, not because my machine was overloaded'; decision workers-sized-per-machine: 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record, and where the machine cannot carry the budget's workers, they write a lowered count with its reason instead of closing blocked', and its rationale names exactly the harm left: 'the first round after it failed 22 tests with services not answering ... Each such failure becomes a fixer task, so an overloaded machine costs fix rounds'; 'A record outside the committed tree changes no other machine's count.' Saw: a machine-independent committed mark suppresses the per-machine fit on every machine but the one whose preflight set it; evidence: the quoted lines of scripts/tests (lines 475-478), skills/plan-sprint/tests.md line 38, scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md lines 609-611.

Reviewed /ok-setup step 3.4 with the budget prompt it runs (skills/plan-sprint/tests-budget.md), then drove it in a scratch project: with no budget recorded, 'tests machine --workers 2 --reason ... --evidence ...' refused: 'tests: --workers 2 is above the budget's 1 workers, which the stack's sizing carries: give a count from 1 to 1'. tests-budget.md says the budget planner 'may write a lowered count for this machine, up to the scenario list's budget, the bound tests machine reads with no sprint. Where the count you propose is larger than that bound and this machine cannot carry it, write nothing, and say in the budget item's body what this machine carries and why: the preflight writes this machine's count once the plan stands.' On a first /ok-setup the scenario list holds no budget, so the bound is 1 and the planner can write no count of 2 or more; /ok-setup's step 3.4 then writes the budget with 'tests budget --from-run' and shows the owner the workers, stack, sizing, files, and limits, and no step reads the count the budget item's body named or writes it with 'tests machine --workers' once the budget stands; it ends with 'The next sprint with test stages runs the preflight against the budget before its first test task.' Until such a sprint, every 'tests run' on this machine runs the budget's full count; after the budget was written I ran 'tests run --from tests.json' and saw 'run: seed 3448492661, 4 workers from the budget' with no record. The story promises: 'a way to have the suite's load fit what my machine can carry, run after run'; decision workers-sized-per-machine: 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record, and where the machine cannot carry the budget's workers, they write a lowered count with its reason instead of closing blocked.' Saw: the budget planner's finding about this machine at /ok-setup is recorded only in an item body that nothing acts on; evidence: the refusal quoted above, tests-budget.md 'Budget' last bullet, ok-setup/SKILL.md step 3.4 lines 97-101.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:move_all (with convert_moving and intake_migration_refusals). move_all records one archived ledger entry per placed file under history/issues/ or history/tensions/ before any move ('if inside(destination, ARCHIVE_DIR): record_archived([path for src, dst in pairs for path in placed_files(src, dst)])', true-up:2812-2813). Trigger: the markdown or tensions intake conversion fails after that write: a git mv failure inside move_all, or import_issues refusing in convert_moving; move_back returns every file to .ok-planner/issues/ and the ledger keeps its entries, since it only appends and no verb clears one. Harm (A3): on every later /ok, intake_migration_refusals computes 'held = [os.path.basename(dst) for _, dst in pairs if archive_held(dst)]' (true-up:2799-2801) and refuses 'the closed-record ledger already lists <names> under .ok-planner/history/issues/', naming no action the owner can take; the conversion can never run again, and while markdown issue files stand every .ok-planner/bin/issues verb refuses with reason layout, saying to run /ok. At the base the refusal read os.path.lexists of the destinations, which move_back had emptied, and move_all recorded nothing. ADMINISTRATION.md:261 states the same refusal. Reports i17, i23.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:## 5. Draft (line 118). The name check counts a sprint name taken only 'where .ok-planner/sprints/ holds a file of that name, or where .ok-planner/bin/review closed --kind sprint --json lists an entry whose name is that file name'. Trigger: the archive holds a sprint an earlier release archived with no closed: stamp; true-up:archive_migration records it as kind archived, name sprints/<file name> (ADMINISTRATION.md:278 'One with no valid stamp gets an archived entry under its archive path'). Planning then takes that file name, and sprint-document.md archive step 7 moves the new sprint and its companions to .ok-planner/history/sprints/ with 'mv for an untracked one', which overwrites the earlier archived sprint and its same-named companions. Harm (A2): a write lands on an archived record. The sibling checks the same change wrote take the archived kind: plan-docs/SKILL.md:43 also counts 'review closed --kind archived --json lists doc-sprints/<that file name>', and discover-design/SKILL.md:27 counts archived discoveries/<name>-base.txt; the sprint check alone omits archived sprints/<file name>. At the base section 5 checked no name. Report i19.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:test_state_conversion. At the base it returned at once where .ok-planner/test-state.json did not stand as a file ('if os.path.islink(TEST_STATE) or not os.path.isfile(TEST_STATE): return None, None'). Now the early return covers only a symlink or a non-file (true-up:5203-5204), so an absent list falls through to tests_command(['convert-state', '--dry-run', ...]) on every true-up; scripts/tests::cmd_convert_state enters state_lock(root) even under --dry-run, and state_lock -> cache_path -> tasks::cache_dir runs os.makedirs(root/.ok-planner/.cache) and writes .ok-planner/.cache/.gitignore and tests-state.lock. Trigger: true-up diagnose in a project with no scenario list, a bootstrap candidate with no .ok-planner/ included. Reproduced in a scratch git repo: diagnose printed 'the plan above; nothing written.' and left .ok-planner/.cache/tests-state.lock and .ok-planner/.cache/.gitignore. Users: ADMINISTRATION.md:12 ('diagnose # read-only'); plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md takes .ok-planner/ as the integration marker and offers bootstrap only where it is absent, and says 'On abort, write nothing'. Old outcome: diagnose wrote nothing. New outcome: the estate marker stands after an aborted bootstrap, so the next /ok takes the project as integrated. The notes' B23 does not list this change. Report i21.

Build fork i106 (t49). The notes decide the shape the code built ('Where move_back undoes a conversion, the entries stay as held names, since the ledger only appends', Pick archive names from the ledger, Calls, Recording), so the fork itself needs no C1/C4. The harm it leaves is A3's: an operator's true-up leaves the product where later use fails. Trigger: the markdown or tensions intake conversion fails after its moves, through true-up:convert_moving -> move_all (which calls record_archived for every placed file under history/issues/ or history/tensions/ before the move; true-up:2812-2813) -> a 'git mv failed' return (e.g. another git command takes the index lock after prechecks) or import_issues refusing at apply -> move_back restores the files and sys.exit. The ledger now lists each name as archived though the archive holds none of them. Every later true-up plans the same conversion with the same destinations, and true-up:intake_migration_refusals (2800-2802) refuses it: 'held = [... for _, dst in pairs if archive_held(dst)]' -> 'the closed-record ledger already lists <names> under .ok-planner/history/issues/'. No verb clears a ledger entry and the message names no action, so the conversion can never run again and every issues verb keeps refusing with reason layout while the markdown intake stands. Scope: caused by the change (record_archived and the ledger-held refusal are new in this sprint; at the base the refusal read os.path.lexists of the destinations, which move_back had emptied).

C2 under A3, from build fork i106 (t49). Trigger: an owner runs /ok on a project whose intake holds markdown issue files under .ok-planner/issues/ (or pre-4.0 tensions), and the conversion's import fails after its dry run passed, or a git mv inside move_all fails. Path: admin/true-up::convert_moving -> move_all, which calls record_archived([...placed files under history/issues/]) before any move (true-up:2811-2813), so the ledger .ok-planner/closed-records.jsonl gains one archived entry per file; the import (or the move) fails; move_back returns every file to .ok-planner/issues/ (true-up:2835) and the ledger keeps its entries, since it only appends and no verb clears one. Next /ok: conversion_refusals -> intake_migration_refusals computes held = [dst for _, dst in pairs if archive_held(dst)] (true-up:2799-2801) and refuses 'the closed-record ledger already lists <names> under .ok-planner/history/issues/'. Harm: the conversion can never run again, and while markdown issue files stand under .ok-planner/issues/ every .ok-planner/bin/issues verb refuses with reason layout, saying to run /ok, so the intake is unusable and /ok cannot clear it; the refusal tells the owner nothing they can do. The corpus decides only that the bookkeeping is written before the move (decision:archive-read-by-nothing: 'Each archive step writes the bookkeeping before it moves a file into the archive'); it does not decide that a held name whose file never landed refuses the same step's rerun. Scope: caused; the ledger, record_archived, and the held check are new in this sprint (absent at 5743a8a).

A2 on the changed Draft name check (build call i97, unlisted). Trigger: the archive holds a sprint an earlier release archived with no closed: stamp; true-up's archive_migration (admin/true-up::archive_migration, lines 4364-4380) records such a file as kind archived, name sprints/<file name>, not as kind sprint. Path: plan-sprint/SKILL.md section 5 now says a name is taken only where .ok-planner/sprints/ holds the file or 'review closed --kind sprint --json' lists it, so the new sprint may take that file name; then sprint-document.md archive step 7 moves the sprint, which planning leaves untracked, to .ok-planner/history/sprints/ with plain mv ('Use git mv for a tracked file and mv for an untracked one'), and mv replaces the archived record of the earlier sprint, with each same-named companion. Harm: an archived record is overwritten. The sibling checks this sprint wrote take the archived kind too: plan-docs/SKILL.md section 5 counts 'review closed --kind archived' doc-sprints/<file name>, and discover-design counts archived discoveries/<name>-base.txt; the sprint check alone omits sprints/<file name> archived entries. Scope: reached; the change added this check at this site, and the overwrite on a colliding name stood at the base, where section 5 checked no name at all.

Before (5743a8a): it returned (None, None) at once where .ok-planner/test-state.json did not stand as a file, so diagnose ran no carried tool in such a project. After: the early return covers only a symlink or a non-file, and an absent list falls through to tests_command(["convert-state", "--dry-run", ...]) on every true-up. scripts/tests::cmd_convert_state enters state_lock(root) even under --dry-run, and state_lock -> cache_path -> review.issues.tasks.cache_dir(root) runs os.makedirs(root/.ok-planner/.cache) and writes .ok-planner/.cache/.gitignore and tests-state.lock. Trigger: a bootstrap candidate (no .ok-planner/) whose owner says yes at step 3, then aborts the plan at step 5; or any diagnose in a project with no scenario list. The estate marker now stands after an abort, so the next /ok takes the project as integrated and skips the bootstrap question. toc_steps, which skips where ok_dir is absent, now also runs catalog-toc --check in that same diagnose. checks/oscillation:close_commits lists .ok-planner/history/sprints through review.ARCHIVED_SPRINTS and reads each archived sprint's closed: stamp with review.closed_stamp (checks/oscillation:34-48: 'archive = os.path.join(ROOT, review.ARCHIVED_SPRINTS)' ... 'stamp = review.closed_stamp(f.read())'). This sprint added decision:archive-read-by-nothing ('No skill, script, hook, or agent reads the archive on its own ... Each fact a tool needs about closed work lives in a live bookkeeping file'), moved the record of each sprint's close into the closed-record ledger (review.closed_records(root, 'sprint'), scripts/review:1908), and the archive step no longer writes a stamp (sprint-document.md:592: 'No step writes a closed: stamp or reads a file under .ok-planner/history/'). Trigger: checks/run after any sprint closes under this release. Harm (A8, the decision's commitment): the check reads the archive on its own, and every sprint closed from now on carries no stamp, so section_churn silently skips it and prints 'oscillation: no section churn in history'. The code stood the same at the base; the change reaches it by removing the stamp it reads and by the new decision. The report's claim that ARCHIVED_SPRINTS is gone does not hold today (scripts/review:79 still defines it), but the archive read stands. From report i3.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:222 (the estate note materialized as .ok-planner/CLAUDE.md) says the owner will 'decide each change no sprint explains'. This sprint renamed that owner decision: plan-docs/SKILL.md:37 now heads it 'A change no closing commit made' (base: 'A change no sprint explains'), and decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window says 'a change no such closing commit made'. The sprint edited the same paragraph (line 220, 'reading the closing commits of the sprints closed since the stamp') and left the old term. Trigger: an agent reads the estate note. Harm (A8, plumbline-coding rule 1: a renamed term left in its old form; the writing standard's one term per thing): the note names the decision by its retired term. From report i5.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:declarations_text builds the verifier brief's lock sentence from the test's own records alone: 'entry = {"locks": declared_locks(s, old)}; recorded_declarations(entry, item); if entry["locks"]: ... return ["It holds no lock, so it is isolated."]' (scripts/tests:5416-5421). It never reads support_lock_map/test_support_locks or the locks pool, and stage_verify never calls live_tests, whose effective_locks (scripts/tests:3083-3098) the run, the round header, the lock check, and tests window use. Trigger: tests tasks --stage verify files a verifier for a tests item whose test lists a test support file that declares locks (test_support_locks or a locks item keyed by the path), or whose scenario gained a lock through a flaky fixer's locks item, while the test's own list is empty. Path: cmd_tasks -> stage_verify -> test_verify_brief -> test_verify_line -> declarations_text. Harm (A9): the brief tells the verifier the test is isolated and holds nothing from its test support, which is false; test-verify.md:29-31 tells the verifier its brief names 'the locks its test support declares', and B4 rules briefs name the test support's locks. Its siblings scenario_brief ('Locks its test support declares: ...', 4741-4742) and speed_brief (entry['support_locks']) name them. Caused by this sprint. From reports i8 (sprint-1) and, in area sprint-3, i6.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:test_support_brief (5129-5146) opens with the file's locks, 'Locks it declares: %s.' from support.get(path), then lists each scenario whose test uses the file with 'lines += ["- %s" % scenario_brief(s) for s in scenarios]' (5140), passing no support_locks. scenario_brief (4722-4744) then prints 'It holds no lock, so it is isolated.' for every such scenario with no own locks. Trigger: tests tasks --stage write files a test support task for a file whose locks the scenario list's test_support_locks or a locks item records, e.g. [{name: notice, mode: exclusive}]. Path: cmd_tasks -> stage_write -> stage_test_support -> test_support_brief -> scenario_brief. Harm (A9): the brief tells the test support writer that the tests which take this file's locks are isolated, contradicting its own first line and decision:tests-isolated-unless-declared ('every test that lists the file as its test support takes them'). Caused by this sprint (the isolation sentence and the support_locks parameter are new). From report i7.

Improvement I1 promises 'declared_locks and merged_locks are the one reader every site calls, so a later change to the declaration edits one function.' plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:declaration_changes (5372-5381) reads the declaration precedence itself: 'planned = next((record["locks"] for record in (s, old) if isinstance(record.get("locks"), list)), None)', the same first-record-holding-a-list rule declared_locks implements (1197-1199), while declarations_text beside it calls declared_locks(s, old) over the same two records. Entry: tests tasks --stage verify -> stage_verify -> test_verify_line -> declaration_changes. Where the outcome ends: a change to how a declaration is read must edit declaration_changes as well as declared_locks, the cost I1 says it removes (C1, an I-id reached only in part; also plumbline-coding rule 6). Caused by this sprint. From report i9.

Work item 'Have writers declare only the locks their tests show' (and B4/B105): skills/converge/prompts/test-verify.md:29-31 tells the verifier its brief names 'the locks the test holds, and the locks its test support declares'. The brief stage_verify files is built by plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:test_verify_line -> declarations_text (5416-5421), which reads only the plan scenario's, the state record's, and the tests item's own locks, never support_lock_map/test_support_locks or the locks pool, and prints 'It holds no lock, so it is isolated.' where the test's own list is empty. stage_verify never calls live_tests, so a lock a flaky fixer's locks item added (B105 names 'the verify brief' among its readers) never shows. Entry: tests tasks --stage verify -> stage_verify -> test_verify_brief -> test_verify_line -> declarations_text; the outcome the work item promises is reached only in part (C1). Same flaw as i51 in area sprint-1. Caused by this sprint. From report i6.

Work item 'Route a flaky test through its round's window' (notes: a stopped round's reproduction, fix.md step 9, uses the round's order seed and worker count too). fix.md:63 (step 9) sends a stopped--silence defect whose tests all pass alone to 'route the cause as the flaky route in step 3 says'. That route (fix.md:41) opens with 'tests window --sprint ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>', and verify.md:49 checks a lock with the same 'tests window ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>'. For a stopped round there is no window: the defect's test is 'stopped--silence', which cmd_window refuses ('round %d of %s planned no test %s'), and each test the round left is recorded by scripts/tests:unreported (3384-3395) with seconds None and not_run, so cmd_window refuses it too via run_timed ('records no run of %s, so it has no window'). Path: fix.md step 9 -> step 3 flaky route -> tests window (refuses) -> race / overload / found-none record -> verify.md flaky bullet -> 'Rerun tests window' (refuses) -> the check cannot hold, so the verifier sends the fix back. A suite defect has no send-back limit, so a stopped round caused by a race between tests that pass alone has no route a verifier can accept: the work item's outcome is not reached for step 9 (C1), and the loop re-files the defect without end. Caused by this sprint. From report i10.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp writes each docspec's state (write_state, state['stamp'] = args.commit) and only then records the close with review.record_closes, which can raise (a malformed ledger, an entry already listed). The sprint names the rerun as the recovery for a stamp that stops before its entry (notes, 'Record a documentation sprint's close in the ledger', Calls; CEREMONY-ARCHIVE resume rule). On the rerun, old_stamp is the closing commit itself, stale_until = parent_commit(args.commit), and 'stale = {claim["id"] for claim in stale_claims(state, set(committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)))}' diffs the closing commit against its parent, so it lists every file the closing commit changed; ledger_after (858-868) then drops each previous claim whose id is stale. Trigger: a stamp that stops after write_state for some or all docspecs and before record_closes, then is run again. Harm (A1): each kept claim whose file or sources the closing commit changed and that this run did not rewrite or recheck is dropped from the claim ledger, though an uninterrupted stamp (old_stamp = the earlier stamp, diffed only up to the parent) keeps it, so the rerun leaves a ledger no complete run produces, and docs window and the next documentation sprint lose those claims. The stale computation stood at the base; the change reaches it by adding the record_closes step after the state writes and naming the rerun as the recovery. From report i11.

Trigger: a project is trued up while a tested sprint is in flight whose run already holds a preflight task closed done under the earlier resources/reads form. Path: admin/true-up::test_state_conversion -> tests:converted_plan drops the plan budget's preflight mark and prints 'its budget's preflight mark %s is dropped, so the sprint's preflight checks the suite command against the locks' (scripts/tests:1641-1651), and locked_list drops the scenario list's mark with 'so the next tested sprint's preflight checks the suite command against the locks' (1569-1573). But tests:stage_preflight (5204-5212) sees the run's last preflight closed done and returns None, so no preflight runs for that sprint, and at the archive step cmd_stamp -> stamped_budget (5986-5992) puts the old preflight's id back on the budget it writes into the scenario list ('budget = dict(budget, preflight=preflights[-1]["id"])'). The next tested sprint whose budget is unchanged then skips its preflight (stage_preflight: 'if plan["budget"].get("preflight") and plan["budget"] == read_state(root)["budget"]: return None'). Harm (A9): the conversion's lines and the testing-suite-command-locks issue true-up files (scripts/tests:5429-5436, 'True-up dropped the budget's preflight mark, so the next tested sprint's preflight checks the suite command against the locks', with the option 'Change the suite command in the next tested sprint's preflight') tell the owner a check will run that never runs on this path. Caused by this sprint (the mark drop and the issue are new; stamped_budget stood at the base and the change reaches it). From report i12.

plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:2477-2481, the citation block above certified_without_config, reads '# @decision: every-stop-ends-the-goal' / '# @decision: sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository' / '# @decision: sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository' / '# @decision: archive-read-by-nothing'. The second sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository line repeats the first; at the base 5743a8a the block held each slug once, and the ledger stage (work item 'Keep the closed-record ledger in the review tool') added the archive-read-by-nothing line beside the copy. Trigger: none at run time; the defect is in the source. Harm (A8, plumbline-cheatsheet Comments: a configured citation tag is written only where a standard directs a link, and every other comment is residue to delete): no standard directs a second tag of the same slug. A scan of the family's scripts and the true-up core for consecutive duplicate citation lines finds only this one. From report i13.

Artifact: decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window, which the work item 'Plan documentation from closing commits' names: 'It asks the owner about a change no such closing commit made'; the work item: 'An unexplained change is a change in the window to what the docspec describes that no listed closing commit made.' Code site: plan-docs/core.md:160-165 (step 5) defines it as 'a change in git diff <stamp> whose files no listed closing commit's git show --name-only names'. What it does instead: it tests file overlap, not which commit made the change. Trigger: a docspec stamped at S; sprint A closes at Z and changes skills/foo/SKILL.md; an out-of-band commit Y after S also changes skills/foo/SKILL.md in a way the docspec describes. git diff S shows the file changed, Z's name-only list names it, so the planner counts Y's change as Z's and returns no unexplained change; /plan-docs's Resolve step ('A change no closing commit made', SKILL.md:37) never asks the owner, and the writers describe Y's change with no owner answer, which the decision reserves to the owner. So a stopped-and-rerun stamp leaves a claim ledger no complete run produces, and docs window's stale count and the next documentation sprint's checkers lose those claims. body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md:"Close the issues the run resolved". What the code does: the owner list closes an intake issue only for a defect with an issue field that stands verified, or for a report with an issue field the merge rejected; it never reads a report at state merged. Trigger: two category: defect issues name one flaw; review backlog adds one report per issue, and the merge (merge.md step 3, and in sprint mode step 4's fold onto a defect that carries an issue field) settles the second report merged onto the first issue's defect, which carries only the first issue id. Harm (A9): the run fixes and verifies the flaw, yet the second issue stays open as category: defect, so the intake tells the owner a fixed defect still stands; the next /plan-sprint offers it at Frame, and a sprint that listed it ends certification with it still open, which the work item 'Sprint certification fixes the defect issues its sprint lists' ('The owner list closes each listed issue whose defect stands verified as fixed') promises against. Evidence: owner-list.md:95 'For every defect with an `issue` field that stands `verified`, close its issue as fixed'; owner-list.md:11 reads 'the rejected reports with an `issue` field, and the reports still `open`'; grep -n merged owner-list.md prints nothing. In scope: the sprint added sprint-mode backlog reports and the fold onto an issue's defect (B409, B410), so a listed issue now reaches this gap. From drive failure i32 (driver t27).

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:"7. Sign-off" step 5. What the code does: it gives the merge's tracker command with the selector unquoted: '.ok-planner/bin/tasks file --role sign-off-merge --prompt sign-off-merge --agent ok-opus --key <key> --consumes verdicts:* prohibitions:open --brief ...' (SKILL.md:227). Trigger: the session runs the line as written in a zsh shell, the shell the Bash tool runs on this machine (SHELL=/bin/zsh). Harm (A3): zsh expands the unmatched glob and stops with 'zsh:1: no matches found: verdicts:*', exit 1, filing nothing, so sign-off cannot file its merge as written and the owner gets no signed-off sprint; under bash the same line files the task. Evidence: SKILL.md:227 quoted above; the driver saw the zsh refusal, bash filing t3, and the quoted form 'verdicts:*' filing t4 under zsh; it is the only unquoted --consumes glob in the family's skills. In scope: the sign-off on the task tracker is new in this sprint (base 5743a8a holds no 'verdicts:*'). From drive failure i35 (driver t31).

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_preflight. What the code does: the write stage files no preflight where the plan's budget carries a preflight mark and equals the budget the scenario list records (scripts/tests:5207 'if plan["budget"].get("preflight") and plan["budget"] == read_state(root)["budget"]'; usage text lines 475-478), and plan-sprint/tests.md step 4 (line 38) carries the recorded budget 'its preflight mark included, and the sprint's test stages run no preflight for a budget the plan leaves as recorded'. The mark sits in the committed .ok-planner/test-state.json, set by whichever machine's preflight last passed, while the worker record is per machine and git-ignored (.ok-planner/.cache/tests-machine.json). Trigger: a sprint with test stages runs on a second developer's machine, or on this machine after .ok-planner/.cache is dropped, with the budget unchanged. Harm (A8, story suite-fits-the-machine-it-runs-on and decision workers-sized-per-machine): no preflight and no budget planner runs, nothing measures the machine or writes its lowered count, and every whole-suite round on that machine runs the budget's full worker count; only the flaky fixer lowers the count after an overload round has already failed tests, the harm the decision's rationale names ('the first round after it failed 22 tests with services not answering'). The story promises 'a way to have the suite's load fit what my machine can carry, run after run'. In scope: the sprint's new story and decision make the per-machine fit a promise, and this committed mark defeats it on every machine but one. From drive failure i39 (driver t42).

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests-budget.md:Budget (last bullet), with plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md step 3.4. What the code does: the budget planner may write a lowered count only up to the scenario list's budget, the bound tests machine reads with no sprint; where its proposed count is larger it writes nothing and says in the budget item's body what this machine carries (tests-budget.md:86-93 'write nothing, and say in the budget item's body what this machine carries and why: the preflight writes this machine's count once the plan stands'). On a first /ok-setup the scenario list holds no budget, so the bound is one worker. /ok-setup step 3.4 then writes the budget with 'tests budget --from-run' and no step reads the count the item's body names or writes it with 'tests machine --workers'. Trigger: a first /ok-setup on a machine that cannot carry the proposed workers. Harm (A8, decision workers-sized-per-machine: 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record, and where the machine cannot carry the budget's workers, they write a lowered count with its reason'): the budget planner's finding is recorded only in an item body nothing acts on, and every 'tests run' on this machine runs the budget's full count until a sprint's preflight runs. Evidence: 'tests machine --workers 2 ...' refused 'tests: --workers 2 is above the budget's 1 workers, which the stack's sizing carries: give a count from 1 to 1'; after the budget was written, 'tests run --from tests.json' printed 'run: seed 3448492661, 4 workers from the budget'. In scope: the per-machine record and the planner's lowered count are new in this sprint. From drive failure i40 (driver t42).

Reviewed /converge (SKILL.md, merge.md, owner-list.md, scripts/review cmd_backlog) for a backlog of two category: defect issues that name one flaw. review backlog adds one report per issue (scripts/review:cmd_backlog). The merge folds the second onto the first's defect: merge.md step 3 'Where it is, add the report's hunt number to that defect's seen ... settle every report: tasks item set <report id> --state merged --note "<defect id>"', step 4 'Join reports of this hunt that name one flaw into one defect', and in sprint mode 'a report on the same flaw as a defect that carries an issue field ... settles onto it and adds no defect'; the defect is added with one '--field issue=<the issue id>'. owner-list.md closes issues only for 'every defect with an issue field that stands verified' and for 'every report with an issue field that the merge rejected'; it reads 'the rejected reports with an issue field, and the reports still open' and never a report at merged. So the folded issue's flaw is fixed and verified, yet its issue stays open as category: defect; the next /plan-sprint offers it to the owner at Frame as an open defect to pick, and a sprint that listed it ends certification with it still open. The story promises: defects found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment; saw: an issue whose defect the run fixed stays in the intake for the owner. Evidence: owner-list.md 'For every defect with an issue field that stands verified, close its issue as fixed: issues close <the issue id> --as fixed --fixed-by <the run's name>'; grep -n merged owner-list.md prints nothing.

Reviewed /plan-sprint section 7 (Sign-off) step 5 and ran its tracker commands against a scratch project trued up from the working tree. The step gives the merge command unquoted: ".ok-planner/bin/tasks file --role sign-off-merge --prompt sign-off-merge --agent ok-opus --key <key> --consumes verdicts:* prohibitions:open --brief ..." (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:227). The story promises a signed-off sprint; the sign-off cannot file its merge as written in the session's shell on this machine (SHELL=/bin/zsh, the shell the Bash tool runs). Saw: under zsh the command exits 1 with 'zsh:1: no matches found: verdicts:*' and files nothing; under bash the same line prints 't3', exit 0; with the glob quoted ('verdicts:*') zsh files the task (t4) and its claim prints only the amend-1 key's verdicts. It is the only --consumes glob in the family's skills (grep of plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills for '--consumes ...:*'). The fix is to quote the selector in the skill text.

Reviewed how a sprint's test stages fit the suite to the machine: the preflight (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/test-preflight.md, Check 1) is the one step that measures this machine before a round and writes a lowered count to .ok-planner/.cache/tests-machine.json; the write stage that files it (scripts/tests help, line 475) says: 'It files no preflight where the plan's budget carries a preflight mark and equals the budget the scenario list records', and plan-sprint/tests.md step 4 (line 38) says: 'the plan carries the recorded budget, its preflight mark included, and the sprint's test stages run no preflight for a budget the plan leaves as recorded.' The mark is committed in .ok-planner/test-state.json and set by whichever machine's preflight last passed, while the machine record is per machine and git-ignored (ok-planner-CLAUDE.md line 609: deleting .ok-planner/.cache drops tests-machine.json, 'so the next bin/tests run runs the budget's worker count'). So on a second developer's machine, or this machine after its cache is dropped, no preflight and no budget planner runs while the budget stands unchanged, nothing measures the machine, and the first whole-suite round runs the budget's full count; only the flaky fixer lowers the count, after an overload round has failed tests. Under testing.enabled frozen no write stage files a preflight at all. The story promises: 'a way to have the suite's load fit what my machine can carry, run after run, so that a test fails for a fault in the product or the test, not because my machine was overloaded'; decision workers-sized-per-machine: 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record, and where the machine cannot carry the budget's workers, they write a lowered count with its reason instead of closing blocked', and its rationale names exactly the harm left: 'the first round after it failed 22 tests with services not answering ... Each such failure becomes a fixer task, so an overloaded machine costs fix rounds'; 'A record outside the committed tree changes no other machine's count.' Saw: a machine-independent committed mark suppresses the per-machine fit on every machine but the one whose preflight set it; evidence: the quoted lines of scripts/tests (lines 475-478), skills/plan-sprint/tests.md line 38, scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md lines 609-611.

Reviewed /ok-setup step 3.4 with the budget prompt it runs (skills/plan-sprint/tests-budget.md), then drove it in a scratch project: with no budget recorded, 'tests machine --workers 2 --reason ... --evidence ...' refused: 'tests: --workers 2 is above the budget's 1 workers, which the stack's sizing carries: give a count from 1 to 1'. tests-budget.md says the budget planner 'may write a lowered count for this machine, up to the scenario list's budget, the bound tests machine reads with no sprint. Where the count you propose is larger than that bound and this machine cannot carry it, write nothing, and say in the budget item's body what this machine carries and why: the preflight writes this machine's count once the plan stands.' On a first /ok-setup the scenario list holds no budget, so the bound is 1 and the planner can write no count of 2 or more; /ok-setup's step 3.4 then writes the budget with 'tests budget --from-run' and shows the owner the workers, stack, sizing, files, and limits, and no step reads the count the budget item's body named or writes it with 'tests machine --workers' once the budget stands; it ends with 'The next sprint with test stages runs the preflight against the budget before its first test task.' Until such a sprint, every 'tests run' on this machine runs the budget's full count; after the budget was written I ran 'tests run --from tests.json' and saw 'run: seed 3448492661, 4 workers from the budget' with no record. The story promises: 'a way to have the suite's load fit what my machine can carry, run after run'; decision workers-sized-per-machine: 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record, and where the machine cannot carry the budget's workers, they write a lowered count with its reason instead of closing blocked.' Saw: the budget planner's finding about this machine at /ok-setup is recorded only in an item body that nothing acts on; evidence: the refusal quoted above, tests-budget.md 'Budget' last bullet, ok-setup/SKILL.md step 3.4 lines 97-101.

Reviewed the fix path a break found by /drive takes. /drive SKILL.md: 'the owner list files each defect the merge keeps in the intake as a category: defect issue, for the next /converge to fix'. The next /converge in defects mode takes it through the backlog; merge.md: 'Merge each real one with --field issue=<the issue id> and its source backlog.' The issue record and its backlog report carry no story, surface, or variant field. converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 6: '6. **Confirm, in drive and sprint mode.**', and scripts/review unconfirmed_drive_defects keeps only a defect whose source is 'drive' (or one a source=drive duplicate folds into). So a drive-found break fixed by /converge defects is closed fixed on a verifier's reading of the change alone, with no driver ever trying the story again. Probed in a scratch true-up of the working tree: filed issue probe-sketch-defect (category defect), review backlog added report i3 {area: backlog, issue: probe-sketch-defect, site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md} with no story field; by contrast a source=drive defect i2 got 'confirm: defect i2; story sketch-an-idea; surface skill:sketch; variant whole; ... confirm 1 of 1' from review drives --confirm. In /converge drive mode the same break is caught again only because the new drive re-finds it as a separate source=drive defect. evidence: review backlog output '{"reports": [{"item": "i3", "issue": "probe-sketch-defect", "files": ["plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md"]}], "settled": []}'; review drives --confirm --dry-run listed only {"defect": "i2", "story": "sketch-an-idea"}.

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's sign-off checklist (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md), the docspec and surface intent definitions (skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md), /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and scripts/docs. Drove .ok-planner/bin/docs window in a scratch project. A reference docspec can name a class under ## Lists that the surface intent's rules name but that has no line under ## Where each class is declared, and sign-off approves it. Then no documentation sprint can list that class's members or find a missing one, and the run still ends DOCS COMPLETE. The sign-off Lists rule asks only that 'each bullet names a class the surface intent names, live or as a delta of the sprint amends it', and the Declaring lines rule checks only that each existing line 'names a class the rules above it name'. No rule requires a declaring line for each class a reference docspec lists. The definition asks for lines only 'for each class of entry point'. Downstream, DOC-CHECK-PROMPT has the checker 'list every public element of each class the docspec's ## Lists names from the files the surface intent names as declaring it'. With no declaring file it lists nothing, so no 'missing: <element>' claim is ever recorded and the completion contract holds. /plan-docs SKILL.md step 2 admits 'the surface intent names no declaring file for the class, so the reference cannot list its members', yet 'An unmatched class leaves the status as it stands', so the run goes ahead, and the class goes back to a /plan-sprint whose checklist has no rule that fires on it. The story promises: 'my reference documentation [names] every element I made public ... so that a reader can depend on what the reference lists'. The artifact definition promises: 'The documentation sprint lists every public element of each class from the tree as it stands, starting from the files the surface intent names as declaring the class'. Saw: a listed public class with no declaring line passes sign-off, and its reference is never checked for completeness. Evidence: a scratch docspec whose ## Lists bullet was '- tool verbs' and whose surface intent declares only '- tool commands: `cli/commands.py`' gave: 'docspec:tool-reference ... status: reached / - listed class matches no declaring line under "## Where each class is declared": tool verbs' (docs window, exit 0), and nothing stops the run.

body: Reviewed the test planning procedure (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests.md) and the sort prompt (tests-sort.md) for a taken legacy folder, then ran the procedure's tool steps in a scratch project (tests offers, groups --take legacy:<folder>, a sort task's items, tests plan, tests tasks --stage write, the legacy tasks' work, tests ports, stamp, rules, rules take): those all worked. The divergence: tests.md step 2 files the sort tasks in the same step as the story and runtime planners, with no --after, and drains them together ('Where the sort list holds files, file one sort task per ten of them ... --brief "<the inputs line>; files: <the paths>"'. 'Drain.'), so sort agents run concurrently with the planners. Yet tests-sort.md Read step 2 tells the sort agent to read 'The scenarios the story planners and the runtime planner recorded: tasks item list --pool scenarios --json' and to sort 'It checks the outcome a recorded scenario states ... adopt, into that scenario'. When the sort agent runs before a story planner records its new scenario, it sees none, and adopts the legacy test 'into a scenario you record' under its own id; the assembly (scripts/tests, the adopted-into-new branch near line 2489) only turns a planner's new scenario into an adopt when the legacy item's scenario field names that new scenario's id, so the plan carries a new scenario and an adopt for one outcome, and a new test gets written beside the legacy test that already checks it, unless the plan-wide review happens to flag the duplicate. The story promises the owner keeps the tests that check what the product promises; decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically states: 'A planned new scenario a legacy test already checks adopts that test in place of a new one.' The procedure leaves that to a race and a judgment review; filing each sort task --after the story and runtime tasks (or a second drain) would make it hold. evidence: tests.md step 2 text quoted above; tasks file accepts --after (usage line: '[--after AFTER [AFTER ...]]'); in the scratch run, an adopt whose scenario id names no planner scenario assembled as its own scenario: 'scenarios: 0 keep, 0 new, 0 rewrite, 0 retire, 0 gap, 1 adopt'.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2a), the sprint execution boilerplate (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 6a), the test-speed, test-verify, and test-write prompts, the shared TEST-SPEED-JUDGING block, and the tests tool's speed verbs (slowest, tasks --stage speed, settled, stamp). The speed read at write time, in the build stages, and after a failed round, the median ranking under the lock bound, acceptances that outlive support changes, product-slow handling, and the verifier's same-outcome check all match the decisions. One divergence: an unsettled speed send-back returned to its last passing version is not carried to the next sprint. SKILL.md step 2a sends the test back with the reason 'return the test file to blob <the blob>, its last passing version: its speed rewrite did not settle, and the speed send-back stays open for the next sprint', and docs/testing.md says the same ('its send-back stays open for the next sprint to take up'). But the tests tool reads speed verdicts only from the current sprint's run and certification ledger (scripts/tests:2996 record_runs returns sibling(sprint, '-run.jsonl') and certification_ledger(root, sprint); speed_runs at 3030 and speed_rows/stage_speed at 5618/5705 read only those), and stamp writes no send-back into .ok-planner/test-state.json (scripts/tests:6062 state.update writes stamps, scenarios, unguarded, budget, inferred, kept, ranking, ranked_sprints, acceptances, reaches, test_support_locks; stamped_acceptances at 5965 keeps accepted verdicts alone). So once the sprint is archived, the next sprint's speed task brief (speed_brief, built from speed_sent_back(merged, sid) over the current sprint's runs only) carries no earlier send-back, and the reader starts with nothing of the waste found. The story promises: the suite sped up over the sprints the owner already runs; decision failed-speed-rewrite-returns-to-its-last-passing-version says 'its send-back stays open for the next sprint to take up' and its rationale 'The open send-back carries the waste the reader found to the next sprint's speed read.' Saw: nothing persists the open send-back across the sprint boundary; the waste a reader found is dropped, and the next sprint picks the test only if the ranking happens to select it, with a fresh brief. evidence: scripts/tests:2997 'return [run for run in (sibling(sprint, "-run.jsonl"), certification_ledger(root, sprint))'; scripts/tests:6062 state.update(...) has no send-back key; skills/converge/SKILL.md:122 'and the speed send-back stays open for the next sprint'.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i55 i57 i71
- i55: Work item 'Route a flaky test through its round's window' (notes: a stopped round's reproduction, fix.md step 9, uses the round's order seed and worker count too). fix.md:63 (step 9) sends a stopped--silence defect whose tests all pass alone to 'route the cause as the flaky route in step 3 says'. That route (fix.md:41) opens with 'tests window --sprint ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>', and verify.md:49 checks a lock with the same 'tests window ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>'. For a stopped round there is no window: the defect's test is 'stopped--silence', which cmd_window refuses ('round %d of %s planned no test %s'), and each test the round left is recorded by scripts/tests:unreported (3384-3395) with seconds None and not_run, so cmd_window refuses it too via run_timed ('records no run of %s, so it has no window'). Path: fix.md step 9 -> step 3 flaky route -> tests window (refuses) -> race / overload / found-none record -> verify.md flaky bullet -> 'Rerun tests window' (refuses) -> the check cannot hold, so the verifier sends the fix back. A suite defect has no send-back limit, so a stopped round caused by a race between tests that pass alone has no route a verifier can accept: the work item's outcome is not reached for step 9 (C1), and the loop re-files the defect without end. Caused by this sprint. From report i10.
- i57: Trigger: a project is trued up while a tested sprint is in flight whose run already holds a preflight task closed done under the earlier resources/reads form. Path: admin/true-up::test_state_conversion -> tests:converted_plan drops the plan budget's preflight mark and prints 'its budget's preflight mark %s is dropped, so the sprint's preflight checks the suite command against the locks' (scripts/tests:1641-1651), and locked_list drops the scenario list's mark with 'so the next tested sprint's preflight checks the suite command against the locks' (1569-1573). But tests:stage_preflight (5204-5212) sees the run's last preflight closed done and returns None, so no preflight runs for that sprint, and at the archive step cmd_stamp -> stamped_budget (5986-5992) puts the old preflight's id back on the budget it writes into the scenario list ('budget = dict(budget, preflight=preflights[-1]["id"])'). The next tested sprint whose budget is unchanged then skips its preflight (stage_preflight: 'if plan["budget"].get("preflight") and plan["budget"] == read_state(root)["budget"]: return None'). Harm (A9): the conversion's lines and the testing-suite-command-locks issue true-up files (scripts/tests:5429-5436, 'True-up dropped the budget's preflight mark, so the next tested sprint's preflight checks the suite command against the locks', with the option 'Change the suite command in the next tested sprint's preflight') tell the owner a check will run that never runs on this path. Caused by this sprint (the mark drop and the issue are new; stamped_budget stood at the base and the change reaches it). From report i12.
- i71: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:stage_preflight. What the code does: the write stage files no preflight where the plan's budget carries a preflight mark and equals the budget the scenario list records (scripts/tests:5207 'if plan["budget"].get("preflight") and plan["budget"] == read_state(root)["budget"]'; usage text lines 475-478), and plan-sprint/tests.md step 4 (line 38) carries the recorded budget 'its preflight mark included, and the sprint's test stages run no preflight for a budget the plan leaves as recorded'. The mark sits in the committed .ok-planner/test-state.json, set by whichever machine's preflight last passed, while the worker record is per machine and git-ignored (.ok-planner/.cache/tests-machine.json). Trigger: a sprint with test stages runs on a second developer's machine, or on this machine after .ok-planner/.cache is dropped, with the budget unchanged. Harm (A8, story suite-fits-the-machine-it-runs-on and decision workers-sized-per-machine): no preflight and no budget planner runs, nothing measures the machine or writes its lowered count, and every whole-suite round on that machine runs the budget's full worker count; only the flaky fixer lowers the count after an overload round has already failed tests, the harm the decision's rationale names ('the first round after it failed 22 tests with services not answering'). The story promises 'a way to have the suite's load fit what my machine can carry, run after run'. In scope: the sprint's new story and decision make the per-machine fit a promise, and this committed mark defeats it on every machine but one. From drive failure i39 (driver t42).
