brief:
fix round 1; defects i56
- i56: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp writes each docspec's state (write_state, state['stamp'] = args.commit) and only then records the close with review.record_closes, which can raise (a malformed ledger, an entry already listed). The sprint names the rerun as the recovery for a stamp that stops before its entry (notes, 'Record a documentation sprint's close in the ledger', Calls; CEREMONY-ARCHIVE resume rule). On the rerun, old_stamp is the closing commit itself, stale_until = parent_commit(args.commit), and 'stale = {claim["id"] for claim in stale_claims(state, set(committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)))}' diffs the closing commit against its parent, so it lists every file the closing commit changed; ledger_after (858-868) then drops each previous claim whose id is stale. Trigger: a stamp that stops after write_state for some or all docspecs and before record_closes, then is run again. Harm (A1): each kept claim whose file or sources the closing commit changed and that this run did not rewrite or recheck is dropped from the claim ledger, though an uninterrupted stamp (old_stamp = the earlier stamp, diffed only up to the parent) keeps it, so the rerun leaves a ledger no complete run produces, and docs window and the next documentation sprint lose those claims. The sprint names the rerun as the recovery for a stamp that stops before its entry (notes, 'Record a documentation sprint's close in the ledger', Calls; CEREMONY-ARCHIVE resume rule). On the rerun, old_stamp is the closing commit itself, stale_until = parent_commit(args.commit), and 'stale = {claim["id"] for claim in stale_claims(state, set(committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)))}' diffs the closing commit against its parent, so it lists every file the closing commit changed; ledger_after (858-868) then drops each previous claim whose id is stale. Trigger: a stamp that stops after write_state for some or all docspecs and before record_closes, then is run again. Harm (A1): each kept claim whose file or sources the closing commit changed and that this run did not rewrite or recheck is dropped from the claim ledger, though an uninterrupted stamp (old_stamp = the earlier stamp, diffed only up to the parent) keeps it, so the rerun leaves a ledger no complete run produces, and docs window and the next documentation sprint lose those claims. The stale computation stood at the base; the change reaches it by adding the record_closes step after the state writes and naming the rerun as the recovery. From report i11.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i60
- i60: B504 and the short-close hold changed the readiness rule in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:open_waits/held_wait (831-843): a wait is met only once its task closed and is no held short close. The work item's usage changes updated the opening paragraph, config set, next, claim, and refile, but two entries still restate the old rule. tasks:136-138, 'tasks task set': '(an `after` that names a task not closed takes an issued, unclaimed task back to unissued in the same write, so `next` issues it once those tasks close)'; cmd_task (1604, 'waits = open_waits(run, t)') also unissues the task where a named dependency is a held short close, which has already closed, and next issues it only once a refile of that dependency closes done. tasks:111-114, 'tasks retry': '... goes back to unissued, so `next` issues it once that task closes'; where the retried task's role is in held_roles and it closes partial or blocked again, held_wait keeps its waiters unissued until a refile exists. Trigger: an orchestrator in a held_roles run reads tasks --help or the review facts to learn when a re-pointed or retried task is issued. Harm (A8, plumbline-coding rule 1: a changed definition and the literals that restate it edited in the same change): the usage and the facts state the retired rule. Caused: the sentences stood true at the base and the change made them false. From report i15.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp writes each docspec's state (write_state, state['stamp'] = args.commit) and only then records the close with review.record_closes, which can raise (a malformed ledger, an entry already listed). The sprint names the rerun as the recovery for a stamp that stops before its entry (notes, 'Record a documentation sprint's close in the ledger', Calls; CEREMONY-ARCHIVE resume rule). On the rerun, old_stamp is the closing commit itself, stale_until = parent_commit(args.commit), and 'stale = {claim["id"] for claim in stale_claims(state, set(committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)))}' diffs the closing commit against its parent, so it lists every file the closing commit changed; ledger_after (858-868) then drops each previous claim whose id is stale. Trigger: a stamp that stops after write_state for some or all docspecs and before record_closes, then is run again. Harm (A1): each kept claim whose file or sources the closing commit changed and that this run did not rewrite or recheck is dropped from the claim ledger, though an uninterrupted stamp (old_stamp = the earlier stamp, diffed only up to the parent) keeps it, so the rerun leaves a ledger no complete run produces, and docs window and the next documentation sprint lose those claims. The stale computation stood at the base; the change reaches it by adding the record_closes step after the state writes and naming the rerun as the recovery. From report i11.
note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp now computes the stamp it will write (new_stamp: the planned commit for a bearing docspec, else --commit) before the stale computation, and computes no stale claims where the docspec's state already carries that stamp, which is the state a stamp that stopped before record_closes wrote. ledger_after is idempotent with no stale ids (I202 drops held ids from kept before re-adding them), so the rerun leaves the same claim ledger the uninterrupted stamp wrote, instead of diffing the closing commit against its parent and dropping every kept claim whose file or sources that commit changed. A first stamp is unchanged: its old stamp is an earlier sprint's. Enumeration: one site, the stale computation in cmd_stamp (rg old_stamp/stale_until/committed_between in scripts/docs; the other committed_between callers, bearing_docspecs and window, read no state this run writes). Lint and checks/run pass. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs.

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp and later_commits_bearing: on a stamp rerun after a stop before record_closes, later_commits_bearing reads each docspec's ledger as the first pass left it. Where the first pass stamped a docspec at the planned commit only because of a stale-claim reason on a claim that pass then dropped (its file deleted, or its recheck cut), the rerun finds the docspec not bearing, stamps it at --commit instead of the planned commit, and diffs planned..parent for stale claims. The guard I built covers old stamp == the stamp the rerun writes; telling this residual case apart from a first stamp whose earlier stamp is this sprint's planned commit needs a marker the state does not carry (for example the sprint name in the doc-state file) or reading the pre-stamp state from the closing commit. Built: the narrow guard only.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests-budget.md:Budget (last bullet), with plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-setup/SKILL.md step 3.4. What the code does: the budget planner may write a lowered count only up to the scenario list's budget, the bound tests machine reads with no sprint; where its proposed count is larger it writes nothing and says in the budget item's body what this machine carries (tests-budget.md:86-93 'write nothing, and say in the budget item's body what this machine carries and why: the preflight writes this machine's count once the plan stands'). On a first /ok-setup the scenario list holds no budget, so the bound is one worker. /ok-setup step 3.4 then writes the budget with 'tests budget --from-run' and no step reads the count the item's body names or writes it with 'tests machine --workers'. Trigger: a first /ok-setup on a machine that cannot carry the proposed workers. Harm (A8, decision workers-sized-per-machine: 'The preflight and the budget planner read the record, and where the machine cannot carry the budget's workers, they write a lowered count with its reason'): the budget planner's finding is recorded only in an item body nothing acts on, and every 'tests run' on this machine runs the budget's full count until a sprint's preflight runs. Evidence: 'tests machine --workers 2 ...' refused 'tests: --workers 2 is above the budget's 1 workers, which the stack's sizing carries: give a count from 1 to 1'; after the budget was written, 'tests run --from tests.json' printed 'run: seed 3448492661, 4 workers from the budget'. In scope: the per-machine record and the planner's lowered count are new in this sprint. From drive failure i40 (driver t42).
note: tests-budget.md: Budget's last bullet and Record now have the budget planner, where the bound leaves it to write nothing, record this machine's count on the budget item as machine_workers, machine_reason, machine_evidence (and in the body), instead of the body alone. ok-setup/SKILL.md 3.4: field_types declares budget.machine_workers integer; after 'tests budget --from-run' writes the budget, the session reads the latest done budget task's item and, where machine_workers is below the budget's workers, runs 'tests machine --workers <n> --reason <r> --evidence <e>' (now in bound, since the budget stands) and tells the owner. So a first /ok-setup's finding reaches this machine's record and tests run uses the lowered count. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up:move_all (with convert_moving and intake_migration_refusals). move_all records one archived ledger entry per placed file under history/issues/ or history/tensions/ before any move ('if inside(destination, ARCHIVE_DIR): record_archived([path for src, dst in pairs for path in placed_files(src, dst)])', true-up:2812-2813). Trigger: the markdown or tensions intake conversion fails after that write: a git mv failure inside move_all, or import_issues refusing in convert_moving; move_back returns every file to .ok-planner/issues/ and the ledger keeps its entries, since it only appends and no verb clears one. Harm (A3): on every later /ok, intake_migration_refusals computes 'held = [os.path.basename(dst) for _, dst in pairs if archive_held(dst)]' (true-up:2799-2801) and refuses 'the closed-record ledger already lists <names> under .ok-planner/history/issues/', naming no action the owner can take; the conversion can never run again, and while markdown issue files stand every .ok-planner/bin/issues verb refuses with reason layout, saying to run /ok. At the base the refusal read os.path.lexists of the destinations, which move_back had emptied, and move_all recorded nothing. ADMINISTRATION.md:261 states the same refusal. Reports i17, i23.
note: Root: the conversion recorded its archived names before the move (archive-read-by-nothing keeps that order) and its rollback left them in the append-only ledger. Fix: scripts/review gains unrecord_closes(root, entries), which removes exactly the named entries under the ledger's lock (closed-records.lock) by atomic replace through issues.write_records. true-up: record_archived now returns the names it recorded ([] where it only notes the pending ledger); convert_moving records them itself (moved out of move_all, its one caller) and, in the move-back branch after move_back, calls the new unrecord_moved_back, which removes each recorded name whose file no longer stands under history/ and prints 'unrecorded: <n> archived name(s) in .ok-planner/closed-records.jsonl, whose files moved back' (ReviewError -> sys.exit as record_entries does). So intake_migration_refusals' held check no longer meets the failed run's names, and a later /ok runs the conversion again. ADMINISTRATION.md: the markdown-intake paragraph now says the step records the names first and removes them for files that moved back; the tensions paragraph says the same; CLAUDE.md layout line names unrecord_closes. Probed in a scratch project with a copy of the core whose real import refuses: recorded 1, moved, moved back, unrecorded 1; a rerun with the real core converted (recorded 1, moved, imported 1). Files: admin/true-up, admin/ADMINISTRATION.md, scripts/review, CLAUDE.md.

body: Work item 'Route a flaky test through its round's window' (notes: a stopped round's reproduction, fix.md step 9, uses the round's order seed and worker count too). fix.md:63 (step 9) sends a stopped--silence defect whose tests all pass alone to 'route the cause as the flaky route in step 3 says'. That route (fix.md:41) opens with 'tests window --sprint ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>', and verify.md:49 checks a lock with the same 'tests window ... --round <the defect's round> --test <the scenario>'. For a stopped round there is no window: the defect's test is 'stopped--silence', which cmd_window refuses ('round %d of %s planned no test %s'), and each test the round left is recorded by scripts/tests:unreported (3384-3395) with seconds None and not_run, so cmd_window refuses it too via run_timed ('records no run of %s, so it has no window'). Path: fix.md step 9 -> step 3 flaky route -> tests window (refuses) -> race / overload / found-none record -> verify.md flaky bullet -> 'Rerun tests window' (refuses) -> the check cannot hold, so the verifier sends the fix back. A suite defect has no send-back limit, so a stopped round caused by a race between tests that pass alone has no route a verifier can accept: the work item's outcome is not reached for step 9 (C1), and the loop re-files the defect without end. Caused by this sprint. From report i10.
note: scripts/tests:window_lines and cmd_window no longer refuse a test the round recorded no times for (a stopped round's not run tests): such a test has no start, so its window lists every test the round ran under 'ran', the latest arrival first, each with its span and the locks it shares in the round and now, and every other untimed test under 'unreported' with its shares; text output prints both groups; usage text for tests window updated. fix.md step 9 now routes an all-pass stopped round through the flaky route with each test the round left with no result in the scenario's place, reads that test's window, reproduces with those tests and their windows at the round's seed and workers, and sets the defect's tests field to those tests. verify.md's flaky-record check now covers a stopped--silence defect, reading the window of each test its tests field names, and the lock check accepts a partner among the ran or untimed tests of such a window. So the race / overload / no-cause records the fixer makes for a stopped round have a window the verifier can rerun. body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp writes each docspec's state (write_state, state['stamp'] = args.commit) and only then records the close with review.record_closes, which can raise (a malformed ledger, an entry already listed). The sprint names the rerun as the recovery for a stamp that stops before its entry (notes, 'Record a documentation sprint's close in the ledger', Calls; CEREMONY-ARCHIVE resume rule). On the rerun, old_stamp is the closing commit itself, stale_until = parent_commit(args.commit), and 'stale = {claim["id"] for claim in stale_claims(state, set(committed_between(root, old_stamp, stale_until)))}' diffs the closing commit against its parent, so it lists every file the closing commit changed; ledger_after (858-868) then drops each previous claim whose id is stale. Trigger: a stamp that stops after write_state for some or all docspecs and before record_closes, then is run again. Harm (A1): each kept claim whose file or sources the closing commit changed and that this run did not rewrite or recheck is dropped from the claim ledger, though an uninterrupted stamp (old_stamp = the earlier stamp, diffed only up to the parent) keeps it, so the rerun leaves a ledger no complete run produces, and docs window and the next documentation sprint lose those claims. The stale computation stood at the base; the change reaches it by adding the record_closes step after the state writes and naming the rerun as the recovery. From report i11.
note: Walked the rerun through cmd_stamp (docs:914-927): for a docspec the first run wrote, old_stamp equals new_stamp, which comes from the same later/args.commit inputs (a non-bearing docspec cannot turn bearing on the rerun, since planned_ledgers reads a ledger that only shrank), so no stale claims are computed; ledger_after with empty stale ids over the written ledger returns it unchanged (kept already passed every filter; held ids are dropped and re-added), so the rerun leaves the uninterrupted stamp's ledger. A docspec the first run did not write keeps its old stamp and takes the old path. A first run is unchanged except where old_stamp equals the new stamp, where nothing changed between the two and no claim is stale, which is right. The not-held/non-commit-base branch now sits under the same guard and keeps the all-stale reading otherwise. No signature changed; no caller to bring along. Lint passes on scripts/docs; checks/run fails only owned-paths, on admin/true-up, outside this change. Noted, not this defect's path: a bearing docspec (stamped at the planned commit) whose bearing rested only on a stale-claim reason from a claim the first run dropped can lose its bearing on the rerun and take new_stamp=--commit, as it did before the fix.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md:"Close the issues the run resolved". What the code does: the owner list closes an intake issue only for a defect with an issue field that stands verified, or for a report with an issue field the merge rejected; it never reads a report at state merged. Trigger: two category: defect issues name one flaw; review backlog adds one report per issue, and the merge (merge.md step 3, and in sprint mode step 4's fold onto a defect that carries an issue field) settles the second report merged onto the first issue's defect, which carries only the first issue id. Harm (A9): the run fixes and verifies the flaw, yet the second issue stays open as category: defect, so the intake tells the owner a fixed defect still stands; the next /plan-sprint offers it at Frame, and a sprint that listed it ends certification with it still open, which the work item 'Sprint certification fixes the defect issues its sprint lists' ('The owner list closes each listed issue whose defect stands verified as fixed') promises against. Evidence: owner-list.md:95 'For every defect with an `issue` field that stands `verified`, close its issue as fixed'; owner-list.md:11 reads 'the rejected reports with an `issue` field, and the reports still `open`'; grep -n merged owner-list.md prints nothing. In scope: the sprint added sprint-mode backlog reports and the fold onto an issue's defect (B409, B410), so a listed issue now reaches this gap. From drive failure i32 (driver t27).

Caused by this sprint (base step 5 read 'no sprint closed since the stamp made or explains'). From report i14.

body: Reviewed the fix path a break found by /drive takes. /drive SKILL.md: 'the owner list files each defect the merge keeps in the intake as a category: defect issue, for the next /converge to fix'. The next /converge in defects mode takes it through the backlog; merge.md: 'Merge each real one with --field issue=<the issue id> and its source backlog.' The issue record and its backlog report carry no story, surface, or variant field. converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 6: '6. **Confirm, in drive and sprint mode.**', and scripts/review unconfirmed_drive_defects keeps only a defect whose source is 'drive' (or one a source=drive duplicate folds into). So a drive-found break fixed by /converge defects is closed fixed on a verifier's reading of the change alone, with no driver ever trying the story again. Probed in a scratch true-up of the working tree: filed issue probe-sketch-defect (category defect), review backlog added report i3 {area: backlog, issue: probe-sketch-defect, site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md} with no story field; by contrast a source=drive defect i2 got 'confirm: defect i2; story sketch-an-idea; surface skill:sketch; variant whole; ... confirm 1 of 1' from review drives --confirm. The story promises: each break the check finds is fixed, so a change that breaks a promise does not reach users unnoticed; decision one-confirm-driver-per-defect, Choice: 'A fix to a drive-found defect that its verifier accepts gets one confirm driver per defect ... the defect is confirmed only where every story it names succeeds, and is sent back otherwise'. Saw: the /drive then /converge defects route fixes a drive-found defect with no confirm driver, so a fix that leaves the story still broken closes the defect issue as fixed. In /converge drive mode the same break is caught again only because the new drive re-finds it as a separate source=drive defect. evidence: review backlog output '{"reports": [{"item": "i3", "issue": "probe-sketch-defect", "files": ["plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/sketch/SKILL.md"]}], "settled": []}'; review drives --confirm --dry-run listed only {"defect": "i2", "story": "sketch-an-idea"}.
note: backlog-drive-defects-skip-confirm-driver

body: In a scratch project (stack up --name find-and-fix-defects-def6eb1e, true-up), opened a converge ledger, filed one category: defect issue, ran review backlog and review merges --source backlog, recorded the backlog merge's count as merge.md's Count section says (area backlog, hunt 1), then ran analysis steps 1 to 4: review areas, review hunts --first, review merges --round, review tally. SKILL.md analysis step 4 says the tally prints 'for each area ... a decision: hunt while the area has had fewer than hunt.min hunts, stop: converged ..., stop: cap' and the return lists 'per area: hunts run, defects, ... and how the area stopped'. scripts/review:tally_report reads every merges item with no --areas filter, so the backlog pseudo-area appears as an area that 'hunts again', though review hunts never files a hunt for it and it never stops. The story promises: defects found and fixed without me, so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment; saw: the tally and the run's return tell the owner an area still hunts after the hunt loop ended. Evidence: review tally printed {'area': 'backlog', 'hunts': 1, 'latest_new': 1, 'defects': 2, 'estimate': None, 'missed': None, 'decision': 'hunt'} beside six file areas at 'stop: converged'; the next review hunts printed 'hunts: 0 task(s) over 0 area(s)'.
note: tally-reports-backlog-as-hunting-area

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md, _sprint/shared.md) and drove its scripts in a scratch project (true-up, two docspecs: usage at docs/usage.md and api 'in code: src/greet.py' with a ## Generator 'python3 -m pydoc src/greet.py ... not committed'). Sprint 1 ran to DOCS COMPLETE, stamp, window current. Then changed the product (--shout), window showed both reached; planned sprint 2 with usage a change item and api carrying the template's line 'No item: nothing its reader sees changed.' (SKILL.md section 5 keeps such a heading so the stamp moves it forward; core.md planner step 2 yields no item for an in-code docspec reached only through a References corpus artifact or the docspec file changing). Ran the boilerplate steps 5-8 as written. Divergence: doc-sprint-document.md step 7 runs a generator only through checker tasks: 'File checker tasks of up to six files each ... The first checker task of a docspec in round 1 also runs its ## Generator command, where its Where starts in code: and that section names one.' A docspec with no item (or only drop items) gets no checker task, so its generator never runs, while Completion contract item 1 requires 'every docspec with a ## Generator command has its run recorded' and artifact-definitions.md says 'A documentation sprint runs the command, and the command must succeed.' Step 8 only says 'work each failure it names', naming no step that files the generator's checker. The story promises: after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands; the run as written cannot reach DOCS COMPLETE unaided. saw: evidence: '.ok-planner/bin/docs complete --sprint .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-20-second.md' printed 'DOCS NOT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/doc-sprints/2026-11-20-second.md' / '- docspec:api names a generator, and no checker recorded its run', exit=2. After I improvised a check task (key api:1:1, generator=true claim held) it printed DOCS COMPLETE, stamp and archive succeeded, and the next window read both docspecs current.
note: docspec-generator-unrun-without-checker

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's sign-off checklist (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md), the docspec and surface intent definitions (skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md), /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and scripts/docs. Drove .ok-planner/bin/docs window in a scratch project. A reference docspec can name a class under ## Lists that the surface intent's rules name but that has no line under ## Where each class is declared, and sign-off approves it. Then no documentation sprint can list that class's members or find a missing one, and the run still ends DOCS COMPLETE. The sign-off Lists rule asks only that 'each bullet names a class the surface intent names, live or as a delta of the sprint amends it', and the Declaring lines rule checks only that each existing line 'names a class the rules above it name'. No rule requires a declaring line for each class a reference docspec lists. The definition asks for lines only 'for each class of entry point'. Downstream, DOC-CHECK-PROMPT has the checker 'list every public element of each class the docspec's ## Lists names from the files the surface intent names as declaring it'. With no declaring file it lists nothing, so no 'missing: <element>' claim is ever recorded and the completion contract holds. /plan-docs SKILL.md step 2 admits 'the surface intent names no declaring file for the class, so the reference cannot list its members', yet 'An unmatched class leaves the status as it stands', so the run goes ahead, and the class goes back to a /plan-sprint whose checklist has no rule that fires on it. The story promises: 'my reference documentation [names] every element I made public ... so that a reader can depend on what the reference lists'. The artifact definition promises: 'The documentation sprint lists every public element of each class from the tree as it stands, starting from the files the surface intent names as declaring the class'. Saw: a listed public class with no declaring line passes sign-off, and its reference is never checked for completeness. Evidence: a scratch docspec whose ## Lists bullet was '- tool verbs' and whose surface intent declares only '- tool commands: `cli/commands.py`' gave: 'docspec:tool-reference ... status: reached / - listed class matches no declaring line under "## Where each class is declared": tool verbs' (docs window, exit 0), and nothing stops the run.
note: sign-off-passes-listed-class-without-declaring-line

body: Reviewed the test planning procedure (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/tests.md) and the sort prompt (tests-sort.md) for a taken legacy folder, then ran the procedure's tool steps in a scratch project (tests offers, groups --take legacy:<folder>, a sort task's items, tests plan, tests tasks --stage write, the legacy tasks' work, tests ports, stamp, rules, rules take): those all worked. The divergence: tests.md step 2 files the sort tasks in the same step as the story and runtime planners, with no --after, and drains them together ('Where the sort list holds files, file one sort task per ten of them ... --brief "<the inputs line>; files: <the paths>"'. 'Drain.'), so sort agents run concurrently with the planners. Yet tests-sort.md Read step 2 tells the sort agent to read 'The scenarios the story planners and the runtime planner recorded: tasks item list --pool scenarios --json' and to sort 'It checks the outcome a recorded scenario states ... adopt, into that scenario'. When the sort agent runs before a story planner records its new scenario, it sees none, and adopts the legacy test 'into a scenario you record' under its own id; the assembly (scripts/tests, the adopted-into-new branch near line 2489) only turns a planner's new scenario into an adopt when the legacy item's scenario field names that new scenario's id, so the plan carries a new scenario and an adopt for one outcome, and a new test gets written beside the legacy test that already checks it, unless the plan-wide review happens to flag the duplicate. The story promises the owner keeps the tests that check what the product promises; decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically states: 'A planned new scenario a legacy test already checks adopts that test in place of a new one.' The procedure leaves that to a race and a judgment review; filing each sort task --after the story and runtime tasks (or a second drain) would make it hold. evidence: tests.md step 2 text quoted above; tasks file accepts --after (usage line: '[--after AFTER [AFTER ...]]'); in the scratch run, an adopt whose scenario id names no planner scenario assembled as its own scenario: 'scenarios: 0 keep, 0 new, 0 rewrite, 0 retire, 0 gap, 1 adopt'.
note: legacy-sort-tasks-race-story-planners

body: Reviewed /converge sprint mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 2 step 2a), the sprint execution boilerplate (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md step 6a), the test-speed, test-verify, and test-write prompts, the shared TEST-SPEED-JUDGING block, and the tests tool's speed verbs (slowest, tasks --stage speed, settled, stamp). The speed read at write time, in the build stages, and after a failed round, the median ranking under the lock bound, acceptances that outlive support changes, product-slow handling, and the verifier's same-outcome check all match the decisions. One divergence: an unsettled speed send-back returned to its last passing version is not carried to the next sprint. SKILL.md step 2a sends the test back with the reason 'return the test file to blob <the blob>, its last passing version: its speed rewrite did not settle, and the speed send-back stays open for the next sprint', and docs/testing.md says the same ('its send-back stays open for the next sprint to take up'). But the tests tool reads speed verdicts only from the current sprint's run and certification ledger (scripts/tests:2996 record_runs returns sibling(sprint, '-run.jsonl') and certification_ledger(root, sprint); speed_runs at 3030 and speed_rows/stage_speed at 5618/5705 read only those), and stamp writes no send-back into .ok-planner/test-state.json (scripts/tests:6062 state.update writes stamps, scenarios, unguarded, budget, inferred, kept, ranking, ranked_sprints, acceptances, reaches, test_support_locks; stamped_acceptances at 5965 keeps accepted verdicts alone). So once the sprint is archived, the next sprint's speed task brief (speed_brief, built from speed_sent_back(merged, sid) over the current sprint's runs only) carries no earlier send-back, and the reader starts with nothing of the waste found. The story promises: the suite sped up over the sprints the owner already runs; decision failed-speed-rewrite-returns-to-its-last-passing-version says 'its send-back stays open for the next sprint to take up' and its rationale 'The open send-back carries the waste the reader found to the next sprint's speed read.' Saw: nothing persists the open send-back across the sprint boundary; the waste a reader found is dropped, and the next sprint picks the test only if the ranking happens to select it, with a fresh brief. evidence: scripts/tests:2997 'return [run for run in (sibling(sprint, "-run.jsonl"), certification_ledger(root, sprint))'; scripts/tests:6062 state.update(...) has no send-back key; skills/converge/SKILL.md:122 'and the speed send-back stays open for the next sprint'.
note: speed-send-back-not-carried-to-next-sprint

body: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_stamp and later_commits_bearing: on a stamp rerun after a stop before record_closes, later_commits_bearing reads each docspec's ledger as the first pass left it. Where the first pass stamped a docspec at the planned commit only because of a stale-claim reason on a claim that pass then dropped (its file deleted, or its recheck cut), the rerun finds the docspec not bearing, stamps it at --commit instead of the planned commit, and diffs planned..parent for stale claims. The guard I built covers old stamp == the stamp the rerun writes; telling this residual case apart from a first stamp whose earlier stamp is this sprint's planned commit needs a marker the state does not carry (for example the sprint name in the doc-state file) or reading the pre-stamp state from the closing commit. Built: the narrow guard only.
note: docs-stamp-rerun-after-dropped-claim
